_readme: Shared corpus for the shortcut-override sanitize rules, which exist twice on purpose:
Rust `sanitize_settings` (src-tauri/src/settings.rs) is the storage authority, and the
the same answer to decide whether a blurred shortcut field is actually dirty. Unifying them
would mean an IPC round trip per keystroke, so this file is the pin instead: BOTH sides read
it - a vitest case in settingsState.test.ts and a cargo test in settings.rs - so a case
added or edited here exercises both implementations, and drift fails on the side that drifted.
JSON has no comments, hence this key; it carries no cases and both readers ignore it.

cases.name: blank entries are dropped, the mode is kept
a mode whose entries are all blank is dropped entirely
an empty array is kept - a deliberately disabled mode, not an absent override
entry order is preserved - the dirty check compares positionally
mixed: every rule at once across four modes
